enunciado: “I ___ my advisor tomorrow at 3 PM.” (it's in your diary, she's expecting you)
explicacion: A fixed personal arrangement with someone else: present continuous for the future.
Timetables and schedules use the present simple, even for the future.
An instant decision or offer made at the moment of speaking: will.

enunciado: “I've already decided: I ___ apply for that job.”
explicacion: A plan decided before speaking: be going to.

enunciado: “This time next year, I ___ in my first job.”
explicacion: An action in progress at a specific future moment: future continuous (will be + -ing).
Be about to + verb = very near future, in a moment.
Be due to + verb = scheduled or expected at a specific time.

enunciado: “As soon as I ___ my degree, I'm going to apply for jobs.”
explicacion: After when, as soon as and by the time we use the present simple, not will.

enunciado: “By the time I ___ university, I will have a job offer.”
explicacion: Time clauses (by the time, when, as soon as) take the present with future meaning.
A prediction based on present evidence (the clouds): be going to.

enunciado: “I ___ help you with your application, I promise.”

explicacion: Near: tomorrow, next week, soon. Distant: next year, someday, eventually. Specific: at 2 PM, on Monday.
